sources.title: Present simple
sources.paraphrase: Third-person singular present verbs take an inflected form; present negatives use do/does with not.
sources.scopeLimit: Form and polarity evidence does not choose a learner’s unprovided intended message.

sources.title: Personal pronouns
sources.paraphrase: The subject/object table distinguishes he/him, she/her and I/me; ordinary imperatives need no overt subject.
sources.scopeLimit: Case form and directly observed role comparisons do not certify every project score.
sources.locator: Editorial subject/object table and imperative exception

sources.title: Modals: deductions about the past
sources.paraphrase: Might with have and a past participle can describe a possible past event.
sources.scopeLimit: It does not establish that an underspecified learner intended the past.
sources.locator: Editorial might have / may have subsection

sources.title: Demonstratives
sources.paraphrase: This/that mark singular reference; these/those mark plural reference and can accompany nouns.
sources.scopeLimit: An inconsistent number-marked input does not reveal which number the learner intended.
sources.locator: Editorial singular/plural descriptions and With nouns section

sources.title: Present continuous
sources.paraphrase: The progressive combines present be with an ing-form; the table pairs they with are.
sources.scopeLimit: Agreement evidence does not invent an event, participant or time.

sources.title: Book: noun and verb
sources.paraphrase: Book has a written-work noun sense and a separate verb sense involving advance reservation.
sources.scopeLimit: A noun occurrence alone does not satisfy a requested reservation-verb target.
sources.locator: Dictionary editorial noun and verb definitions

sources.title: Help: noun and verb
sources.paraphrase: Help has an assistance noun sense; the dictionary includes a give-help example.
sources.scopeLimit: Combine lexical evidence with imperative syntax; do not infer every collocation is natural.
sources.locator: Editorial noun entry and Kids Definition noun example

sources.title: Music
sources.paraphrase: The dictionary identifies music as a noun for musical sounds and related art.
sources.scopeLimit: A noun’s lexical meaning does not supply a speaker’s missing complete proposition or command.

sources.title: Talking about the future
sources.paraphrase: The future section permits might for uncertain future possibilities, followed by a base-form predicate.
sources.scopeLimit: This possible reading does not identify the intended time of the torch input.

sources.title: Ellipsis and substitution
sources.paraphrase: The publisher’s chapter extract explains situational ellipsis, including short answers recoverable from a question.
sources.scopeLimit: Recoverable answer context must be supplied; the extract does not license an invented command or certify this bank.
sources.locator: Public publisher Summary/extract only, not full chapter
